Lisandro Martinez's Quick Red Card Deepens Manchester United's Struggles Under Michael Carrick

01 Nov 2026, 10:42 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

2 min read

Key takeawaysManchester United faced further pressure following a defeat at Stamford Bridge, where defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off during a costly 83-second sequence that left Michael Carrick's side with 10 men.

Manchester United faced further pressure following a defeat at Stamford Bridge, where defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off during a costly 83-second sequence that left Michael Carrick's side with 10 men.

The Incident at Stamford Bridge

With Chelsea leading 1-0 following a second-half goal by Morgan Rogers, the match turned decisively during a brief spell. Martinez, who was already on a yellow card, attempted to block Wesley Fofana at the far post during a corner. Video assistant referee James Bell advised referee Peter Bankes to review the incident on the pitchside monitor, leading to a second yellow card and a penalty concession for a reckless challenge.

Former World Cup final official Darren Cann described the action to BBC Sport as inexplicable, noting that the defender made no attempt to play the ball. As a result of the red card, Martinez faces a suspension for the upcoming Premier League fixture against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

Match Context and Team Struggles

Reporting indicates that United had shown an improved performance in the first half compared to recent losses against Como and Bournemouth, creating multiple opportunities through Bruno Fernandes and Amad that were either missed or saved by Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders.

However, the defeat extends United's winless run across all competitions to nine matches, marking their worst sequence since the 1989 season. The team is also preparing to host Roma at Old Trafford in a fixture that carries significance for their Champions League qualification hopes.

Analyst Reactions and Verification

Pundits offered strong criticism following the match:

  • Stephen Warnock noted to BBC Sport that falling 2-0 behind with 10 men effectively ended the competitive contest.
  • Joe Cole suggested on TNT Sports that the defender's time at the club may have run its course.
  • Danny Murphy told BBC Radio 5 Live that the mindset of the player was currently unsuitable for selection.

When asked after the match if he felt let down, Carrick stated he had not yet reviewed the incident on video, while emphasizing that the second goal and the red card heavily influenced the outcome. Supporters and observers can verify the official match statistics, disciplinary records, and upcoming fixture details through the Premier League's official channels or accredited sports broadcasting networks.
